findings.reason: the clause needs its own rule for source-anchored design findings (attribute them from the finding text or hold them on the document unit deliberately) and the fourth arm must be built from a real design-record anchor; without both, the one node implementing s13 produces a gate that blocks every section — the defect the section was written to fix.
findings.text: s13 says the existing `_anchor_unit` "maps a finding's anchor to the unit it names, or to the document unit when it names none" and that design-review findings are grouped "the same way", but a real design record anchors to source files by line: `plan-the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches.v5.json` (rubric `design`) carries `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1264`, `reckon/crew/ticker.py:2138` and `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:567`. Reproduced against that plan's own text with the shipped `_anchor_unit`: `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1264 -> _document`, `reckon/crew/ticker.py:2138 -> _document`, `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:567 -> s66` (line 567 of the plan file happens to fall inside that plan's §66, a section unrelated to that source line), while `…html#s5 -> s5`. So "the same way" either blocks every section (two of three anchors) or refuses an unrelated section (the third), which is precisely the plan-wide behaviour s13 exists to remove, and the done-when's fourth arm can only be written by hand-fabricating a `#s4` anchor that no design review produces, so it passes while the shipped grouping misattributes every source-anchored design finding.
